quote: person can find a pin to edit, unpin or quarantine.
problem: The Pins surface offers to quarantine a pin, but Quarantine and I5 apply only to an event, run, writer or derived artifact. Nothing says what quarantining a pin excludes (its creating event, one version's event, or every version), or what then restores. That leaves I3's 'restored verbatim' open: when a later version's event is quarantined, one implementer restores the prior version and another drops the pin. It also leaves open whether reverting to an older version counts as cut or widening.
fix: Add to Quarantine: "Quarantining a pin quarantines every version event of the pin and takes it out of restore blocks (widening when it restores); quarantining one version's event makes the newest unquarantined version restore, and that change is widening."

quote: only changes a cut act could make, never removing a pin from a restore block,
problem: A cut act 'only stops, narrows or undoes a widening', yet removing a pin from a restore block is widening 'whatever verb carries it'. Nothing classes a settings change that stops a restore path (turning `restore_block.on_prompt` off) or shrinks the pin budget. So a repository's untrusted `.parinn.toml`, which takes effect without acceptance, may or may not be able to withhold the principal's constraints from the agent, depending on the implementer.
fix: Add to Principal act's widening list and to repository configuration: "any change that turns off a restore path or lowers the pin budget is widening, and repository configuration never makes one".

quote: and counted (Pin); an author's own pin, edit and unpin act only on pins that
problem: 'Pins that do not restore' could mean pins of a non-restoring type (Pin type says only `constraint` and `preference` pins restore) or pins that do not qualify. That decides whether an agent's run seat may pin a `constraint` or `preference` pin at all. It also decides whether the restore block's count of restoring-type pins that do not qualify can ever be non-zero.
fix: Say "only on pins that do not qualify (a run seat may pin any type; its pins never qualify)", or "only on pins of a type that does not restore", whichever is intended.

quote: is its first version's, and only it, or for a device-seat pin its author's
problem: Pin says only the pin's author (or, for a device-seat pin, its principal) edits it, and Unpin says only the author or its principal unpins it. The Contributor pin capability, however, lets a run seat edit and unpin pins written by the run seats it replaced in the same run.
fix: Change to "and only it, a run seat that replaced it in the same run, or for a device-seat pin its author's principal, edits the pin", and make the same change in Unpin.

quote: authored by its device seat on that node (PIN-01); any other act on
problem: "Any other act on one is refused" covers quarantining a configuration pin's creating or version event. I5 says any event can be quarantined, and Principal act classes 'quarantine that removes a pin from a restore block' as a permitted widening act.
fix: Narrow it to "any other act that adds, edits or unpins one is refused and counted (I6); quarantine applies as to any event".

quote: writer of each run that wrote meanwhile, then move its ingest position past
problem: A run that starts and ends while capture is off never gets a seat or writer, so it gets no capture-gap marker and Runs does not show it. That breaks I1's 'each such stretch shown as a capture gap'. Because a run gets its personal-room seat from its first recorded event, and pins restore only to runs that have a seat in the room (PIN-10), it is also unstated whether a run started while capture is off receives restore blocks.
fix: State that a run started while capture is off still gets its personal-room seat (and restore blocks), with a capture-gap marker as its first event. Runs found in transcript.roots that ran wholly inside the gap get the same.

quote: Each recall tool's name, description and schema, and the MCP server's
problem: The harness hands the tool definitions and the MCP server's instructions to the model without any recall call. They are neither restore blocks nor compaction guidance. That contradicts I2's 'No other write to an agent exists' and I4's exhaustive list of what ParleyInn's components send off the machine.
fix: Add "the MCP server's fixed instructions and tool definitions, fixed text ParleyInn ships" to I2's closed paths and to Closed path, or state that serving them is not a write to an agent.

quote: any other seat belongs to another principal, kept as theirs and untrusted (I8).
problem: A principal has a personal room 'on each of its nodes', and each node's device key certifies only its own seats. By this rule, the same principal's seat from its other node belongs to 'another principal', which misattributes ownership and 'the room's principals'.
fix: Say "any other seat is kept as another node's or principal's, attributed to its seat key and untrusted (I8)".

quote: **Room**: seats and pins. The unit ParleyInn shows and shares.
problem: The only room in this candidate is the personal room, which 'stays private', and I4 (B0 only) gives no path for sharing. 'The unit ParleyInn ... shares' therefore contradicts Personal room and has no mechanism behind it.

quote: its text: ids, kinds, counts, tool names, key fingerprints, addresses, version
problem: Tool names are chosen by MCP servers and paths by files or tool output, which I2 lists as untrusted origins. Once sanitized, the candidate makes both trusted whatever the event's trust level, and restore blocks ('among other things') and compaction guidance may carry trusted structural fields. That lets text an attacker chose, such as a file named like an instruction, reach the model outside any envelope. Sanitizing cannot remove meaning from a name without destroying the name.
fix: Add: "Restore blocks and compaction guidance take only ids, kinds, counts, addresses, key fingerprints and version numbers; tool names and paths, though sanitized, reach the model only through recall."

quote: `operator` event its device seat's seal covers, told apart from a room act by
problem: A principal act is authenticated only by its device seat's writer seal plus a surface mark that the writer itself sets. Processes the harness starts also append to and seal that same writer with the same key: the core seals 'every other writer', the hook handlers create the personal room at first start, and the core records events with no run, writer-label assignments and refused segments. So the record cannot tell an act taken at a principal surface from an operator event that a harness-started process sealed.
fix: State that a principal act carries a signature by a key that only a principal surface loads, never a process the harness started, and that the trust policy counts an operator event as a principal act only with that signature.

quote: changes harness configuration only through explicit install and uninstall
problem: Install is neither a principal act nor a device seat's room act, and the candidate exempts creating the personal room from the principal-surface rule. So nothing refuses `parinn install` from a run's tool process. A prompt-injected agent can change harness configuration, for example by re-pointing the hooks at a fresh home that holds no pins. That drops every constraint from restore blocks without the widening act the candidate requires for removing a pin.
fix: Add: "install and uninstall run only at a principal surface, through the harness's own plugin install or through the managed install path; from a process the harness started they are refused and counted (I6)."

quote: or TUI call from inside a run is the agent's own tool call: never a principal
problem: Recall covers only CLI or TUI calls 'from inside a run', while the principal-surface exclusion covers every process the harness starts (hook commands, status lines). A CLI read called from a hook command is therefore neither a principal surface nor recall, and nothing says its output is enveloped. The harness can feed hook output into the model's context.
fix: Add: "Any CLI or TUI call from a process the harness started, other than ParleyInn's own hook handlers, MCP server and harness strip, is recall: enveloped, whatever its output."

quote: writer of each run that wrote meanwhile, then move its ingest position past
problem: A run that begins and ends while capture is off never gets a writer, so it never receives a capture-gap marker and appears nowhere. I1 nonetheless says 'each such stretch shown as a capture gap'. Nothing states how the gap is shown for such runs, so the loss is silent per run.
fix: Add: "The capture-off and capture-on acts together show the node-wide gap on Runs and Health, covering runs that began and ended within it."

quote: (Record), authored by its device seat on that node (PIN-01); any other act on
problem: The rule 'any other act on one is refused' also refuses quarantining a configuration pin. That contradicts I5, under which any event can be quarantined immediately. Bad pin text that was accepted from a tampered configuration file could then only leave restore blocks through a new configuration acceptance.
fix: Change to "any other pin, edit or unpin act on one is refused and counted (I6); it may be quarantined like any event."

quote: - **Room**: seats and pins. The unit ParleyInn shows and shares.
problem: Nothing in this candidate shares a room. The only room is the personal room, which "stays private", and I4 declares only B0, so no other node or principal can reach it. 'Shares' therefore names a capability nothing can use, and so does 'held by any node' in Writer.
fix: Room: seats and pins in one home; the unit ParleyInn shows. (In Writer, change 'held by any node' to 'held by the node that wrote it'.)

quote: `.parinn.toml`, its **repository configuration**, declares no pins and may make
problem: The candidate never says which repository's .parinn.toml applies to which runs, or at what scope its cut-only changes take effect (node, room or run). The Git group defines no repository concept. One implementer could apply a cloned repository's file node-wide, narrowing settings for unrelated runs. Another could apply it only to runs working in that repository.
fix: Add: "It applies only to runs whose working directory lies in that repository, and only to settings keys scoped to those runs."

quote: **Setup:** configuration and harness configuration, every change shown as
problem: Setup is indented as a child of Health, so it is unclear whether the closed set of room-view surfaces has three members (Runs, Pins, Health, with Setup inside Health) or four. Implementers would build different surface sets.
fix: Outdent Setup to a sibling of Runs, Pins and Health, so the closed set reads: Runs, Pins, Health, Setup.

problem: Principal is defined as "A person", so Person names the same thing a second time and has no use of its own. Its qualifier 'human' implies non-human principals, which the candidate lacks. That breaks the hub's rule that every concept has one name.
fix: Drop the Person entry and use 'principal' wherever the candidate means one, or define Principal as 'the person whose home a node is' and remove Person.
